$comment: What every key on the page is for. Sections describe where a group of strings appears; notes single out the ones constrained by something other than meaning. Read with GLOSSARY.md.

sections.meta:
Never seen on the page. These are the search result, the browser tab, and the card that appears when the address is pasted into a chat application. They are the only reason anyone finds the site at all, so they are written for search rather than translated word for word.

Write what somebody in this language would actually type into a search engine when they have a drive their Mac will not open. That is rarely a literal translation of the English: work out the ordinary phrasing for 'open', 'drive', 'disk', 'read and write' and 'encrypted' in this language and use those words. Keep BitLocker, NTFS, LUKS, macOS and Mac in Latin script — people search for those exactly as they are written, in every language.
sections.ui: Controls in the header, and the link that lets a keyboard reader skip the navigation. Read aloud by screen readers, so they must say what the control does rather than name it cleverly.
sections.nav: The three header links. Features and How it works match headings further down and should use the same words as those headings; Download goes straight to the releases page.
sections.hero: The first screen. One claim, one sentence explaining it, the download link, and a technical line set in a monospace face.
sections.how: Section 01. Why a Linux virtual machine is involved, and three short steps.
sections.features: Section 02, in prose. Three short paragraphs saying what the application does. Plain statements of fact — no superlatives, no selling. The points that matter are that it takes physical drives and image files alike, that BitLocker opens with either a password or a recovery key, and that BitLocker and NTFS are written as well as read.
sections.formats: The table inside section 02: everything the application opens, grouped into encryption, filesystems and disk images, with a Read and a Write column, and a list of what is not supported. Format names are never translated.
sections.name: The last section on the page. One paragraph explaining the name, taken from the application's README.
sections.faq: Six questions about Lukotta, each naming it and asking what it does. They are questions about this application, not general questions about macOS, and the answers say what the application does rather than explaining the surrounding technology. Short: a yes or a no, then one or two sentences. They are published as structured data as well as shown on the page, so a search engine may show an answer directly, which is why every answer has to stand on its own without the question.
sections.footer: Three links, and the copyright and licence line beneath them.

notes.meta.title: At or under 60 characters — search results cut it off, and the count is characters, not words. Put the thing being searched for first and the name Lukotta last. Not a literal translation: the words most likely to be typed, in the order they would be typed.
notes.meta.description: Between 70 and 165 characters. It does not decide ranking, but it decides whether somebody clicks, so it should answer the question the searcher had. Name the formats, say the drive opens in Finder, and say it reads and writes. Keep the product names in Latin script.
notes.meta.ogTitle: The card title when the address is shared in a message. May be shorter and less formal than meta.title, and needs no keywords.
notes.meta.imageAlt: Describes the Lukotta application icon, which is the shared card image. Read aloud by screen readers.
notes.ui.skipToContent: The first thing a keyboard reader reaches. Must say plainly that it skips to the page content.
notes.ui.toTop: The spoken name of the logo, which is a link back to the top of the page.
notes.ui.switchToLight: The appearance switch's spoken name while the page is dark. It names what clicking will do, not what the page currently is.
notes.ui.switchToDark: The same switch while the page is light.
notes.hero.title: The one sentence the page is built around. Keep the full stop.
notes.hero.meta: Set in a monospace face at a small size. Contains {version}, which becomes the released version number. Keep the middle dots as separators.
notes.formats.lead: Introduces the table. The phrase 'will and will not write' is deliberate: the table has rows that are read but never written.
notes.formats.col.read: A column heading, set in capitals in a monospace face. One word if the language allows.
notes.formats.col.write: The same. These two headings sit above columns of ticks and dashes.
notes.formats.yes: Never shown on screen. It is the spoken text behind a tick, for a reader using a screen reader.
notes.formats.vmdkStream.note: Explains why this one format is read but not written. Factual, not a warning.
notes.formats.vhdx.note: The same. The application says so before the image opens, which is worth keeping.
notes.formats.specs: The whole string is a link to SPECS.md. It reads as a sentence, not as a button.
notes.formats.not.body: A list of what cannot be opened, separated by full stops. Each item is a distinct reason; keep them distinct.
notes.how.lead: Sits below the three steps, explaining why a Linux virtual machine is involved at all. Three sentences: macOS cannot, Linux can, so a small Linux machine does it.
notes.footer.copyright: Contains {copyleft}, which becomes a reversed copyright sign, and {year} and {author}, which become the year and a link to the author's own site. All three must survive, spelled exactly as they are. There is no full stop at the end.
notes.footer.gpl: The licence line. GNU General Public License is a proper name and is not translated, though the surrounding sentence is.
notes.name.body: One paragraph. Contains {lukko} and {tta}, which become the Finnish word lukko and the Finnish ending -tta. Both are Finnish and stay as they are in every language; the placeholders must survive, spelled exactly as they are, and the sentence around them is translated.
notes.name.stress: About where the stress falls when the word is said aloud. The page shows this by setting the first syllable apart, so the sentence and the picture must agree.
notes.features.lead: One sentence saying what the application does. Flat and factual; it is not a slogan.
notes.features.body: The three facts that matter most: physical drives and image files alike, BitLocker by password or by recovery key, and BitLocker and NTFS written as well as read. All three must survive translation.
notes.features.body2: Read-only opening and reopening after a restart, mentioned once at the end rather than given their own headings.
notes.formats.not.5: A single item ending in a list of three examples after a colon.
notes.faq.1.a: The first of two paragraphs: that it costs nothing, and that none of the usual paid arrangements apply.
notes.faq.2.a: Both halves matter: that it opens, and that it writes. The volume password and the 48-digit recovery key are two separate ways in and both must survive.
notes.faq.4.a: Filesystem names are never translated. Do not add a list of distributions.
notes.faq.6.a: Says plainly that Intel Macs are not supported. Do not soften it.
notes.faq.1.a2: The second paragraph, about the licence. GNU General Public License is a proper name and is not translated, though the sentence around it is. Free software here means the licence, not the price — the price was the paragraph before. Where a language distinguishes the two senses of free, use the word for the licence.
notes.faq.3.a: The point is writing, not reading. Keep 'onto ... as well as off it', which is what distinguishes this from what macOS already does.
notes.formats.exfat.note: These are handled by macOS itself rather than by the Linux virtual machine, which is why the table marks them differently. Same sentence as the raw image row.
notes.formats.raw.note: Same sentence as the exFAT row, and it should read identically in this language too.
notes.footer.source: Links to the source code on GitHub. One word if the language allows.
notes.meta.ogDescription: The card text when the address is shared. Written for a person who has been sent a link, not for a search engine.
notes.formats.experimental: The footnote under the table, marked by an asterisk against the disk image formats whose drivers were written for Lukotta rather than borrowed. It is a plain statement of fact about how well tested the writing side is, not a warning and not an apology. Do not sharpen it into either.
